rows.note: Use 耳仔 as the all-purpose colloquial noun for the physical ear.

example.english: A mosquito bit my ear and it swelled up.
example.traditional: 我隻耳仔俾蚊咬到腫晒。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zek3 ji5 zai2 bei2 man1 ngaau5 dou2 zung2 saai3

rows.note: Use 聽覺 for the hearing faculty or perception of sound, rather than the body part.

example.english: I have a sensitive ear and can hear even the slightest sound.
example.traditional: 我嘅聽覺好敏感，少少聲都聽到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ge3 ting1 gok3 hou2 man5 gam2 siu2 siu2 seng1 dou1 teng1 dou2

rows.note: Use 樂感 for the musical sensitivity or taste meant by having a good ear for music.

example.english: They have a good ear for music and can catch the beat the first time they hear a song.
example.traditional: 佢好有樂感，第一次聽首歌就捉到個拍子。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 jau5 ngok6 gam2 dai6 jat1 ci3 teng1 sau2 go1 zau6 zuk1 dou2 go3 paak3 zi2
